text:
Alice N.: Ok team - we need to kick off cloud account + VNet scaffolding for a new APAC region (southeastasia) to support upcoming GPU capacity for customer X. Can infra-cloud own subscription creation and initial VNet layout?

Ben K.: I can take subscription + vnet scaffolding. Question: are we doing a new management/landing subscription per region or use the existing apac landing subscription?

Carla O.: We should reuse the landing-zone subscription for shared infra (log analytics, dns, nat), but create a dedicated 'redwood-prod-apac-1' subscription for workloads & GPUs to keep billing and quotas isolated. :+1:

Alice N.: Agreed. High level runbook: 1) create subscription 2) enable policies & tagging 3) create resource groups 4) scaffold VNet with non-overlapping CIDRs 5) bootstrap Terraform remote state 6) deploy shared services (Log / KeyVault / NAT / Bastion) 7) validate connectivity & quotas 8) handoff to provisioning SREs.

Ben K.: CIDR proposal: use 10.200.0.0/16 for the region. Split into: 10.200.0.0/20 - infra (bastion, jump, natgw), 10.200.16.0/20 - compute (gpu nodes), 10.200.32.0/20 - services (db, redis), 10.200.48.0/22 - pods (if using flat). Anyone object? Need to ensure no overlap with customer's VPCs we peer to.

Dan S.: Security notes: KeyVault must have private endpoint in infra subnet, purge protection + RBAC enabled. NSG rules should be default-deny, allow only management CIDR + Azure monitoring. Also require Azure Policy to enforce tags: team, cost-center, environment.

Carla O.: Quotas: request GPU VM quota increases early. For ND A100_v4 on azure (for our A100 workload) request quota in region via support ticket - mention exact VM series (Standard_ND96asr_v4 or similar). Also enable Accelerated Networking on compute subnet.

Ben K.: Terraform bits to bootstrap state (example):
```
resource "azurerm_storage_account" "tfstate" {
  name                     = "rwinfaptfst${var.region_suffix}"
  resource_group_name      = azurerm_resource_group.rg.name
  account_tier             = "Standard"
  account_replication_type = "LRS"
}
```
Initialize remote backend with the storage account and a container called `tfstate`. Create a service principal `sp-infra-apac-1` and grant `Storage Blob Data Contributor` + `Contributor` on the subscription for bootstrap only.

Alice N.: Remind: do NOT give SP owner at subscription scope. We'll use short-lived creds for bootstrap then recorded in vault. Carla please create KeyVault access policy for our CI identity.

Carla O.: Will do. Also set up diagnostic settings to send activity logs & resource logs to central Log Analytics in landing subscription and to the central storage account for billing export. We'll wire up audit sinks for NSG flow logs.

Ben K.: Network peering plan: peer prod subscription VNet to landing shared-services VNet (DNS + NAT + LB). Use service endpoints / private endpoints for storage and KeyVault. Add route table for compute subnet: default route to NAT gateway in infra subnet for controlled egress.

Dan S.: For inbound: only allow SSH from corporate VPN + AWS VPN peer for ops. Use Azure Bastion in infra RG; no public IPs on nodes. For kube API access, restrict control plane to jump IPs and private endpoints.

Alice N.: Validation checklist before handoff to provisioning SREs: 
- Subscription created + tags/policies applied
- Remote TF backend healthy and locked
- VNet + subnets deployed, NSGs associated
- NAT gateway attached and egress tested (curl to httpbin)
- KeyVault private endpoint up and access from CI verified
- Quota increases confirmed (GPU VM capacity)
- Log Analytics workspace subscription ingestion verified
- Billing export shows subscription in billing account
- Peering routes show connected (az network vnet peering show)
- Sample GPU VM booted and `nvidia-smi` returns drivers

Ben K.: I'll run a quick smoke before handoff: spin one Standard_ND96asr_v4 spot + one standard non-GPU to verify routing. Test commands:
```
# verify GPU visible
ssh jump@<bastion-ip> 
az vm run-command invoke -g rg -n gpu-test --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "nvidia-smi"
```

Carla O.: Cost note: GPUs are expensive in this region; flag to finance for potential reserved instance vs sustained use discount. Also enable budget alert with action group to #eng-costs.

Dan S.: Don't forget KMS/HSM integration - create CMK in central key vault or customer-managed key in landing subscription. Add policy to require CMK for storage accounts and disk encryption.

bootstrap-bot: ACTION CREATED - ticket INFRA-APAC-001 created for subscription provisioning (assignee: Ben K.). Link: https://tickets.redwood/infas/INFRA-APAC-001

Alice N.: Great. Ben - please post the final terraform workspace name and the PR link. Carla - confirm quotas ticket number once submitted. I'll schedule a 30m handoff call with provisioning SREs after validation. :calendar: 

Ben K.: Will do. Draft workspace: `apac-1-prod` and state container `rwinf-tfstate-apac1`. PR in ~30m.

Carla O.: Quota ticket submitted: AZURE-QUOTA-76213. Requested 30x Standard_ND96asr_v4. ETA 72h.

Alice N.: Awesome — leaving the thread open for outputs. If anything blocks, ping me.

Ben K.: PR up: https://git.redwood/infra/terra/pulls/418 - contains RG, storage account, vnet, subnets, nsg, tf backend.

Carla O.: Verified diagnostic settings and KeyVault access from CI. Logs flowing to central LA workspace.

Ben K.: Smoke test complete: GPU VM boots, `nvidia-smi` OK, outbound curl works via NAT, peering routes active. Handoff ready.

Alice N.: Closing thread: moving to handoff meeting at 15:00 UTC. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
